name: Meta Infotech Ltd
title: Meta Infotech Ltd - 544441 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY26 PAT fell to INR11 crore from INR14 crore and H2 PAT was INR0.4 crore; management guides only an aspirational 4x PAT by FY29 with no numeric FY27 guidance, and attributes the miss to a vendor sale and FX.

guidance.quote: we have outlined an aspirational aspiration to grow profit after tax by up to 4x from FY26 levels to FY29
we are expecting by March '27, we should be minimum of 350. Between 350 to 375.
We're still expecting INR10 crores overall.

summary.headline: Meta Infotech FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR270 crore but PAT fell to INR11 crore; management targets 4x PAT by FY29 with no numeric guidance.
summary.overview: FY26 was described as an investment year: revenue grew 23% YoY to INR270 crore and H2 revenue grew 72% YoY to INR60 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR18 crore (FY25: INR25 crore) and PAT fell to INR11 crore (FY25: INR14 crore). Management attributed the squeeze to new hires, geographic expansion, 12 new vendor onboardings, a Thales-owned Imperva transition that cut professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore to INR2 crore, and a forex loss on a large contract. The company set an aspirational target of up to 4x PAT by FY29 from FY26 levels, without numeric revenue or margin guidance. Order book stood at INR506 crore as of May 2026, about 1.9x FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: FY26 services revenue was about INR36 crore versus INR35 crore in FY25, roughly 13% of total revenue; services contributed 75% of FY26 EBIT. Management targets at least 25% growth in services revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Product / trading
segments.commentary: Product business, including the large low-margin deal, carried H2 product EBIT loss versus about 8.2% product EBIT margin in H1 per an analyst's reading; management said it will decline product deals below 5-6% margin and target 9-10% going forward.

guidance_outlook: Aspirational target to grow PAT up to 4x from FY26 levels by FY29, described as a three-year plan starting FY27; no revenue or margin numbers given on compliance grounds.
PAT margin to rise above 10% from about 4% currently; management said ex the large low-margin order, PAT margin would already exceed 10%.
Services mix expected to rise from about 13% toward 25-30% of revenue over three years.
Imperva/Thales professional services expected at about INR10 crore in FY27 (INR6-7 crore Imperva, about INR3 crore Thales).
Headcount expected at 350-375 by March 2027; intends to add about 50 engineers per year.
Contracts to be signed on a Spot+2 forex basis going forward to avoid INR-price variability.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose from 265 (Mar-25) to 309 (Mar-26); share of core technical staff increased from about 50% to 90%.
Added around 40-45 people during the year, mostly engineers and mid-senior staff, plus six senior hires with 17-33 years' experience.
Offices now in Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad; Pune expected in one to two months.
In-house paid training centres in Mumbai and Hyderabad (three-month programme) feed fresh hires; Jetking tie-up used for three-year-bond resources.
Dubai: three projects running, one a three-year contract; Gulf, Australia, APAC and US expansion planned.
demand_pricing: Order book INR506 crore as of May 2026 (about 1.9x FY26 revenue), management said to execute over about three years.
Large single contract above INR100 crore (vendor Zscaler) is recognised mainly in H1; management said it would not have taken this order at its margin given a choice, and it dilutes PAT margin.
Largest customer, a private bank, was about 50-55% of FY26 revenue per management; other customers mostly below INR10 crore each.
Forex: INR rate moved from about INR80-85 to INR88-89 per USD on the large deal, causing a loss of a couple of crore; management said this was a one-time item.
Vendor base expanded to about 10 vendors with 12 added in FY26 (8 focused); two more PS partner agreements expected to be signed.
India cybersecurity market cited at USD6-7 billion, growing 15-18% YoY (management estimate).

qa_highlights.question: Why does H2 revenue dip versus H1 each year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to one large Zscaler-linked order above INR100 crore recognised mainly in H1, with billing timing also affected by forex-related delays.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the drop in Imperva services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Imperva was acquired by Thales; the existing team left, cutting Meta's professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore in FY25 to INR2 crore in FY26, versus an expected INR10 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 product EBIT negative and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would check the H2 segment numbers; it stated a policy to avoid product deals below 5-6% margin and to target 9-10% product margins.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow weak versus PBT; is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Paresh Soni said it is timing: about INR20 crore of inventory at March, expected to sell in April; tax payments also weighed on operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company need more equity or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no extra funding is needed for growth; the IPO was not required for expansion, and it cited delayed billing from forex-linked contracts.

risks_watch: Thales/Imperva PS revenue recovery: FY27 expectation of about INR10 crore depends on the new owner's team ramping up; management cited a one-to-one-and-a-half-year gestation period.
Margin dilution from the large low-margin Zscaler-linked contract running for about three years.
Cash conversion: management attributed weak operating cash flow to inventory of about INR20 crore at March and tax outflows; no reconciliation was given.
Attrition: management cited under 20% in FY26 versus 25-40% industry; a 15-25 person bench is maintained.
Customer concentration: largest bank was about 50-55% of FY26 revenue.
Management declined to give numeric revenue or margin guidance on compliance grounds; PAT target of INR40-45 crore by FY29 was an analyst's extrapolation, not confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the three-year plan, but defensive on FY26 results, attributing the profit decline to one-off factors. Evasive on specific numbers, repeatedly citing compliance limits when asked for FY27 revenue, margins and H2 product losses.
key_quotes: So whatever happened before IPO and what is going to happen after the IPO over last six months, of course, there is a dip in overall revenue and stuff like that, which is conscious decision we have taken.
Our gross profit was INR49 crores in '25-'26 and '24-'25. We maintained the same.
So, all our contracts is conversion agnostic. So, customers we are signing up as Spot Plus 2.
Yes, there is a dip. That's a fact and we are not hiding the fact.
